sites.quote: Link-local prefixes MUST NOT be advertised using this TLV.
As is described in [RFC5305]: "The up/down bit SHALL be set to 0 when a prefix is first injected into IS-IS.
sites.reason: The sentence is inside a verbatim quotation of RFC 5305 that the text introduces with 'As is described in [RFC5305]:'; the up/down bit obligation is RFC 5305's, and RFC 5308 repeats it for the reader.

sites.quote: If a prefix is advertised from a higher level to a lower level (e.g. level 2 to level 1), the bit SHALL be set to 1, indicating that the prefix has traveled down the hierarchy.
sites.reason: Second sentence of the same verbatim RFC 5305 quotation opened by 'As is described in [RFC5305]:' and closed after 'i.e., to lower levels'; the up/down bit obligation belongs to RFC 5305.

sites.quote: If the prefix was distributed into IS-IS from another routing protocol, the external bit SHALL be set to 1.
Just as in [RFC5305], if a prefix is advertised with a metric larger than MAX_V6_PATH_METRIC (0xFE000000), this prefix MUST not be considered during the normal Shortest Path First (SPF) computation.
For Hello PDUs, the "Interface Address" TLV MUST contain only the link-local IPv6 addresses assigned to the interface that is sending the Hello.
For LSPs, the "Interface Address" TLVs MUST contain only the non-link-local IPv6 addresses assigned to the IS.
As with [RFC1195] and IPv4, if the IS supports IPv6 routing using IS-IS, it MUST advertise this in the "NLPID" TLV by adding the IPv6 NLPID.
If, during the SPF, a path metric would exceed MAX_V6_PATH_METRIC, it SHALL be considered to be MAX_V6_PATH_METRIC.
The order of preference between paths for a given prefix MUST be modified to consider the up/down bit.
